title: Intelligence is reaching the same goal by different means, including in morphogenesis

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Intelligence is reaching the same goal by different means, including in morphogenesis

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin defines intelligence, following William James, as the ability to reach the same goal by different means; for tissues this is the problem-solving competency to adapt to conditions in order to construct and repair a specific morphology or function, a functional definition that lets intelligence be studied in non-neural substrates.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Intelligence Below the Cellular Level

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I define intelligence here in William James’ [22] sense as the ability to reach the same goal by different means: the focus is on problem‐solving competency, which in this case is the ability to adapt to conditions to construct and repair a specific morphology or function.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Intelligence Below the Cellular Level”. Scope: Any biological system, from molecular networks to organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-03: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.19

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Morphogenetic flexibility is empirically measurable, but the equivalence between that flexibility and intelligence is a chosen usage. Data cannot distinguish the definition from a non-cognitive description of the same behaviour.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The statement stipulates a functional definition of intelligence; observations can measure reaching a goal by different means but cannot confirm that this property should be called intelligence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Alternative terminology predicts identical observations.

The central statement is definitional.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: William James's formulation is adopted here as the meaning of intelligence, including for morphogenesis. Data can show that a tissue reaches one anatomy by more than one route, and that result illustrates the definition rather than testing it. The claim has no empirical truth condition.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The text defines intelligence as reaching the same goal by different means. A definition is not confirmed or refuted by observing that some systems do so.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim states a definition rather than an empirical generalization.

Goal and different means become empirical only after a further operational choice the definition does not fix.
